newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil still chronically weak.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil still chronically weak.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel oil continued its chronic weakness on Tuesday, with refiners preferring cheap crude and little U.S. interest in the product, traders said.

Prices were slightly weaker in northern Europe, with offer levels around $98 fob. Traders said $94 was being bid on Monday but added it appeared to be an attempt to chase levels lower. Availability was reported good.
"It's a right old dog of a market but we hope it has just about hit the bottom," said one trader.
Straight-run fuel markets were a little livelier in the Mediterranean, though prices were hard to pin down.
A cargo of Russian low sulphur loading ex Tuapse 9-10/4 was still being offered and there were Russian M-100s seen available mid-April.
A Turkish high sulphur straight-run of good quality was heard offered at around $88 fob. A cargo of West African straight-run was also heard placed.
